**The paper doesn't report GPU-hours for PPO training of the 175B model, or for any model.**

The closest figure is training compute in petaflop/s-days, on page 17:

- **175B PPO-ptx model:** 60 petaflops/s-days
- **175B SFT model:** 4.9 petaflops/s-days
- **GPT-3 pretraining:** 3,640 petaflops/s-days, for comparison

The paper uses these numbers to argue that "the cost of increasing model alignment is modest relative to pretraining" (p. 17). Note that the 60 petaflops/s-days figure is for PPO-ptx (PPO with pretraining gradients mixed in), not plain PPO.

You can't convert this to GPU-hours from the paper alone. It doesn't say what hardware was used, how many GPUs, or how efficiently they ran.

The paper does give some related training details:

- All RL models were trained for 256k episodes, covering about 31k unique prompts (p. 42).
- Batch size was 512, with a minibatch size of 64 (p. 42).
- For PPO-ptx, they used 8 times as many pretraining examples as RL training episodes (p. 42). This roughly doubles training time compared with training without the pretraining mix (p. 58).
